In detail

Casa de Campo park has a long, well-documented history of street prostitution stretching back over a decade, covered repeatedly by local outlets and the subject of a formal citizen petition. In 2025 a wave of robberies targeting cars and visitors in parking areas was reported, including a first-person victim account. From around 2020 onward, resident complaints of robberies, threats and assaults were also linked to a former minors' shelter near the park. Daytime family/jogger use is largely uneventful, but night-time concerns are well documented. Sources checked: Telemadrid, 'Prostitucion en la Casa de Campo' series; Decide Madrid citizen petition; Telemadrid & El Espanol, Jun 2025 (robbery wave); Vozpopuli, 2020-2021.

Frequently asked questions

Is Casa de Campo safe?

Wandroz currently rates Casa de Campo in Madrid as roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Madrid during the day and an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Madrid at night. This comes from a structured local-source assessment: an area-level review of credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — consolidated across sources rather than taken from a single report. Madrid publishes no comparable neighbourhood-level crime dataset; where a city does, Wandroz uses it instead.

Is Casa de Campo safe at night?

At night, Casa de Campo is rated as an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Madrid. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Casa de Campo a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Casa de Campo's day rating (roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Madrid) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late.
